title: Entitlement & Quota Policies with Graceful Fallbacks (PRD)
creator: Asha Patel
description: This PRD defines entitlement and quota primitives for Redwood Dedicated customers plus a standardized graceful fallback behavior when reserved capacity is exhausted. The goal is to provide deterministic resource guarantees while enabling safe, transparent degradation and cost predictability when customers burst or capacity constraints occur.
problem_statement: Enterprise customers require clear, enforceable entitlements for reserved GPU capacity (monthly/committed pools) and deterministic behavior when demand exceeds those entitlements. Current behavior is ad hoc: some bursts succeed, some requests queue or fail, and customers and SREs lack consistent signals and controls. This causes customer confusion, support overhead, and unpredictable cost/latency outcomes.
objectives: 1) Define entitlement primitives (hard cap, soft quota with warnings, guaranteed throughput, and spillover policies). 2) Specify fallback strategies (model tier downgrade, shared-pool routing, queued retry with timeouts, or rejection with clear error codes). 3) Build API and Console surface for configuring entitlements and viewing usage + forecast. 4) Ensure billing alignment and telemetry for chargeback and SLO reporting.
out_of_scope: autoscaling heuristics and low-level scheduler optimizations (covered by runtime team), enterprise legal contract changes, and non-dedicated hosted API quota management.
requirements: R1: Entitlement primitives must support: committed units (vGPU-hours), concurrent request limits, sustained throughput (tokens/sec), and burst window sizing (duration and burst tokens).

R2: Each entitlement must have a policy that defines one of: No Spillover (hard cap), Allow Spillover to Shared at Cost Premium, Replay to Lower-Capacity Model, Queue With Priority Window, or Reject with Informative Error. Policies are configurable per-customer and per-reservation.
R3: Soft quotas: system should emit proactive alerts when usage reaches configurable thresholds (70%, 90%). Alerts must be visible in Console and emit webhook events to customer integrations.
R4: Fallback actions must be deterministic, documented, and accompanied by telemetry tags so downstream metrics attribute behavior to fallback reason and policy.
R5: API: create/update/get entitlement resources. Console must show live utilization, forecasted burn rate, and recommended tuning hints from Redwood Optimize.
R6: Billing: usage in spillover mode must be billed at a distinct SKU and appear on the invoice with clear line items and attribution to the originating entitlement.

R7: Security & Compliance: entitlement changes must be auditable (who/when), require RBAC-based approvals for >=X changes, and respect KMS key usage for any customer-supplied artifacts in Private deployments.
R8: Migration: provide a one-click mapping of existing reserved pools to new entitlement objects and backward-compatible behavior for customers not adopting the new API immediately.
R9: Observability: standard traces and logs must include entitlement_id, fallback_policy, and remaining_quota_at_request for every request served under dedicated capacity.
R10: Owners: PM owns product spec, Runtime/Serving owns enforcement hooks, Billing owns invoice SKU mapping, Console owns UI surface.
R11: Acceptance and rollout must include a canary phase where 5 pilot customers use the feature behind feature flag for one billing cycle.
R12: Documentation: public docs and migration guide must be written prior to GA and include example policy configs and recommended defaults for small/medium/large customers.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Create, read, update, delete API for entitlement resources works end-to-end and returns correct HTTP codes and validation errors for invalid policies.
AC2: Console shows live utilization within 30s of state change and displays recommended tuning hints when forecasted burn rate crosses thresholds.

AC3: For a customer configured with 'Allow Spillover to Shared at Cost Premium', when dedicated capacity is exhausted, requests are routed to shared-hosted capacity and billed to the spillover SKU; traces include entitlement_id and fallback_policy and latency increase observed is within SLO for spillover routing.

AC4: For 'No Spillover (hard cap)' policy, excess requests are rejected with standardized error code DEDICATED_CAPACITY_EXCEEDED and response includes guidance link and remaining_quota value in response metadata.
AC5: Soft quota alerts trigger at configured thresholds and send webhook and Console notifications; pilot customers confirm alerts within the canary window.
AC6: Billing displays spillover usage as separate line-items and reconciles to telemetry within 0.5% for pilot customers across a billing window.
AC7: Entitlement change events are captured in audit logs with actor, timestamp, diffs, and are queryable via Console activity feed.
AC8: Migration tool maps existing reserved pools to entitlement objects without losing historical usage; rollback path documented and tested in staging.
AC9: Security review for entitlement management completed and any required hardening tasks closed before broad rollout.
AC10: Three pilot customers complete a billing cycle with feature enabled and provide sign-off (usability and clarity of fallback behavior and billing).
ux_considerations: Console UX must make entitlements discoverable on the customer's dedicated capacity page. Primary surfacing: a horizontal bar showing committed vs used vs forecasted consumption, an action button to edit policies, and drill-down to recent fallback events with example request ids. Provide copy templates for error messages: succinct user-facing text and a link to account settings to request quota adjustments.
api_spec: Primary resources: /v1/entitlements (POST/GET), /v1/entitlements/{id} (GET/PATCH/DELETE), /v1/entitlements/{id}/events (GET). Entitlement object fields: name, reserved_vgpu_hours, concurrent_limit, sustained_tokens_per_sec, burst_window_seconds, burst_tokens, fallback_policy (enum), soft_thresholds (list of percents), billing_sku_id, tags. PATCH supports partial updates and returns 200 with new state. APIs must return structured errors with code and human_message.
data_model_changes: Add Entitlement table with columns: entitlement_id, customer_id, reservation_id (nullable), reserved_units, concurrency_limit, burst_policy_json (string), fallback_policy (string), billing_sku, created_by, created_at, updated_at. Backfill script required to migrate reserved_pool ids to entitlement_id mapping.
security_compliance: All entitlement modification endpoints require platform-auth and RBAC checks. High-impact changes (increase >50% of committed units or enable spillover) require an approval workflow that is logged and emailed to billing and security contacts. Ensure audit logs are forwarded to customer's log sink for Private deployments.
rollout_and_migration: Phase 0: internal alpha with test accounts and simulated load. Phase 1: pilot with 3 customers (opt-in) behind feature flag for one billing cycle. Phase 2: open opt-in for all Dedicated customers with migration tooling in Console. Phase 3: GA and defaulting existing reserved pools to mapped entitlements after 90-day notice. Provide automated migration CLI and rollback steps.
success_metrics: SM1: Reduction in Tier1 support tickets for 'unexpected capacity' by 60% within 3 months of GA.
SM2: 95% accuracy between telemetry-reported spillover usage and billing line-items for pilot customers.
SM3: At least 30% of active Dedicated customers opt into entitlements within first quarter after GA.
SM4: Mean time to detect and surface capacity threshold crossing in Console under 60s.
SM5: No security incidents related to entitlement changes in the first 6 months post-GA.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Unsafe billing mismatches leading to customer disputes. Mitigation: run simultaneous dry-run billing for pilot customers and reconcile daily; freeze GA until reconciliations are within tolerance.

Risk: Runtime enforcement bugs could silently allow oversubscription. Mitigation: add runtime asserts and an emergency hard-kill switch and require integration tests that simulate contention scenarios.

Risk: Customers misconfigure permissive spillover and incur unexpected charges. Mitigation: default policies to No Spillover for new entitlements and require explicit opt-in for paid spillover; surface cost estimates before toggling.
Risk: Complexity in Console causes cognitive overload. Mitigation: provide three opinionated presets (Conservative, Balanced, Aggressive) with recommended defaults and one-click apply.
Risk: RBAC gaps allow unauthorized changes. Mitigation: require 2-step approval for high-impact edits and audit log retention for 1 year.
dependencies: ENG-4120: Runtime hooks for entitlement enforcement
ENG-4299: Telemetry tagging for entitlement_id and fallback_policy
ENG-4412: Billing SKU plumbing for spillover charges
ENG-4530: Console widgets for utilization and alerts
SEC-108: Approval workflow and audit log pipeline
timeline: 8 weeks from kickoff: 2w design & API, 3w implementation (runtime + billing + console), 2w pilot/canary, 1w GA prep & docs.
notes: We should coordinate closely with Redwood Optimize to provide recommended defaults for burst sizing. Consider offering an 'auto-fallback' mode that only triggers for traffic patterns matching previous safe bursts; that can be a future extension (post-GA).
open_questions: Q1: What is the default billing multiplier for spillover in contracts that predate SKU pricing?
Q2: Should we support per-route entitlements (route-level reservations) in v1 or defer to v2?
Q3: How long should we retain entitlement change audit logs for trial customers vs enterprise?
Q4: For Private deployments, do customers require a local-only fallback option (e.g., queue-only) rather than routing to shared-hosted?
review_feedback: Initial review from Runtime team requested more deterministic preemption semantics; billing asked for a 0.5% reconciliation tolerance for pilot; Security requested RBAC gating on spillover enablement and that is now included.
qa_plan: End-to-end integration tests in staging with injected contention scenarios, billing dry-run for pilot customers, and manual verification of Console alerts and audit logs. Include chaos test that toggles feature flag during traffic spike.
customer_notes: Pilot customers will receive a migration checklist and estimated monthly cost impact if spillover is enabled. We will schedule 1:1 migration support calls for the three pilot customers.
